It builds each commit in a temporary index on the tip it read. It publishes with `git update-ref refs/heads/athena/records <new> <expected>`, using the all-zero id for the first commit, so every update is a compare-and-swap and a fast-forward. A rejected swap re-reads the tip, re-checks the files against it, rebuilds and retries, up to 8 attempts with a short backoff, then returns `RecordsError::Contended`. The branch is append-only. A `Put` with different bytes at an existing path, any `Delete`, any `Rename`, bad paths and file/directory clashes are all refused, and the whole batch is checked first. A same-bytes `Put` at an existing path is a documented no-op: no commit, and the current tip comes back. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] and records-history.md §8.2 note the writer as built. No crate was added, and nothing outside athena-git calls the writer.
